title: Enterprise procurement probe: mapping model-resilience triggers and fallback decision canvas
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Background: Enterprise customers frequently ask for predictable fallback behavior and procurement triggers when a primary inference provider/model degrades or becomes unavailable. Current product docs describe generic fallback patterns, but we lack an evidence-led decision canvas that maps real procurement thresholds (latency, cost, availability) to specific fallback actions (quantized variants, alternate model family, reserved capacity).

Scope: Run a focused research and prototyping sprint to produce a decision canvas and a prioritized list of model-resilience triggers for enterprise customers. Deliverables will include: 1) an evidence-backed procurement trigger matrix, 2) a scoring rubric for fallback quality vs. cost, 3) 3 field interviews with enterprise buyers to validate thresholds, 4) a set of proposed console controls (UI + API) and telemetry queries for alerting.

Goals: 1) Reduce ambiguity in enterprise procurement conversations by providing deterministic fallback policy recommendations. 2) Identify top 3 procurement triggers that would convert a Reserved/Dedicated purchase or accelerate Private adoption. 3) Produce a roll-forward plan for runtime and Console features to support the canvas.
acceptance_criteria: Procurement trigger matrix (CSV) with at least 6 triggers and documented rationale for each
Fallback scoring rubric tested on 4 model variants and baseline unit-cost comparisons documented
Three recorded buyer interviews with enterprise customers and a synthesis doc summarizing thresholds and quotes
Console prototype screens and API contract draft for setting automated fallback policies
List of required telemetry queries and dashboard mockups for SRE/Customer Success to monitor triggers
updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting with stakeholders. Agreed scope narrowed to procurement triggers that directly influence reserved capacity decisions. Action: Dana to validate feasibility of telemetry queries (ETA 2025-02-18).
2025-02-18: Dana Morales submitted a short feasibility note: KV cache telemetry exists but needs a production-safe sampling flag. Created ENG ticket ENG-28750 to add sampling.

2025-02-20: Data pull PR opened to extract historical latency/cost per-model by customer segment. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/procurement-probe/pull/42. Initial sample shows 3 model families dominate enterprise spend.

2025-02-24: Synthesized draft scoring rubric (quality delta vs cost delta). Shared with Ethan for review. Ethan suggested adding prompt-sensitivity axis to account for hallucination risk under quantized fallbacks. Action: update rubric by 2025-02-28.

2025-02-28: Completed first-pass procurement trigger matrix (attached in Drive). Filters included: 95th percentile tail latency, percent-of-requests over SLA, token-unit price delta, and model availability windows.
2025-03-01: Scheduled buyer interviews: 3 enterprise interviews arranged for week of 2025-03-09. Nora to lead interview guide.
2025-03-03: Design sync: Design asked for two Console flows (policy creation modal + per-model fallback preview). Design has 2-week runway; prototype expected by 2025-03-17.
2025-03-05: PM review with Growth & Sales to align language for procurement playbook. Sales requested a one-page decision sheet for AE enablement. Adding as explicit deliverable.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive automatic fallback reduces tail-cost but can increase regression risk. Recommendation is to pair any automated fallback with prompt-set based quality monitors.
We will surface fallback options in the Console with estimated unit cost delta and an expected quality impact band (Low/Medium/High) — qualitative until we run quant experiments.
Field interviews should prioritize customers with both Hosted and Dedicated usage to observe differences in procurement behavior.
